HOW TO MEASURE
Aim the green circle at the lamp from canopy height, select the matching lamp icon and wait for a stable value. The lamp illustration glows more brightly as more light is measured.

RECOMMENDED PPFD AT CANOPY HEIGHT
Cuttings and seedlings: 100–300 µmol/m²/s
Vegetative growth: 300–600 µmol/m²/s
Flowering without added CO₂: 600–1,000 µmol/m²/s
Intensive flowering with controlled CO₂: 1,000–1,500 µmol/m²/s
Above 1,500 µmol/m²/s: risk of light stress.

APPROXIMATE LUX BY LAMP TYPE
The four ranges below follow the same order: seedlings · vegetative · flowering · intensive flowering.

Full-spectrum LED
7,000–20,000 · 20,000–40,000 · 40,000–67,000 · 67,000–100,000 lux

Purple/blurple LED
4,000–12,000 · 12,000–24,000 · 24,000–40,000 · 40,000–60,000 lux
Lux is less reliable for purple light.

Sunlight
5,400–16,200 · 16,200–32,400 · 32,400–54,100 · 54,100–81,100 lux

Modern sodium/HPS
8,300–25,000 · 25,000–50,000 · 50,000–83,000 · 83,000–125,000 lux

Fluorescent/CFL
7,700–23,000 · 23,000–46,000 · 46,000–77,000 · 77,000–115,000 lux
The highest ranges are generally impractical with fluorescent/CFL lamps.

TYPICAL TOTAL LAMP OUTPUT (PPF)
Modern LED, about 2.5–3.0 µmol/J
100 W: 250–300 · 200 W: 500–600 · 300 W: 750–900 · 480 W: 1,200–1,440 · 600 W: 1,500–1,800 · 720 W: 1,800–2,160 µmol/s

Modern HPS/sodium, about 1.7–2.1 µmol/J
250 W: 425–525 · 400 W: 680–840 · 600 W: 1,020–1,260 · 1,000 W: 1,700–2,100 µmol/s

Fluorescent/CFL, about 0.8–1.3 µmol/J
55 W: 44–72 · 110 W: 88–143 · 220 W: 176–286 · 330 W: 264–429 µmol/s

Lux measures visible light per square metre. PPFD estimates light reaching the plants. PPF is total lamp output. Lumens equal lux × the illuminated area in m². Camera measurements and conversions are indicative; distance, spectrum, reflector and calibration affect the result. Calibrate against a reliable meter and never look directly into powerful grow lights.

HOW TO MEASURE
Choose the front or rear camera and aim the green circle at the lamp from canopy height. Hold the phone still and wait for a stable value. Never look directly into a powerful grow light.

Choose automatic detection to estimate the lamp type. Phone camera filters differ, so calibrate against a reliable meter for more accurate results.

WHAT DO THE VALUES MEAN?
Lux measures visible light per square metre. Foot-candle (fc) is the same measurement in imperial units: 1 fc = 10.7639 lux. PPFD estimates plant-usable light photons. Lumens describe total visible light output: lumens = lux × illuminated area in m².

TARGETS AT CANOPY HEIGHT
PPFD is the preferred plant-light value. Lux and fc are estimates for white full-spectrum LEDs.

Cuttings and seedlings
100–300 µmol/m²/s · 7,000–20,000 lux · 650–1,860 fc

Vegetative growth
300–600 µmol/m²/s · 20,000–40,000 lux · 1,860–3,720 fc

Flowering without added CO₂
600–1,000 µmol/m²/s · 40,000–67,000 lux · 3,720–6,225 fc

Intensive flowering with controlled CO₂
1,000–1,500 µmol/m²/s · 67,000–100,000 lux · 6,225–9,290 fc

TYPICAL MODERN LED OUTPUT
At roughly 2.5–3.0 µmol/J efficiency:
100 W: 250–300 µmol/s PPF
200 W: 500–600 µmol/s PPF
300 W: 750–900 µmol/s PPF
480 W: 1,200–1,440 µmol/s PPF
600 W: 1,500–1,800 µmol/s PPF
720 W: 1,800–2,160 µmol/s PPF

PPF is total lamp output; PPFD is what reaches the plant. Distance, dimming, reflection and area can substantially change the result.
